title: EELS Mapping to Reveal the Spatial Distribution of Cation Valance and Oxygen Deficiency at the Cation-disordered Oxide Cathode
content: Among various candidates as cathode for rechargeable lithium-ion battery, Li-excess and cation-disordered rocksalts (DRX) have recently emerged as a new promising class of high-energy-density cathode materials, which do not rely on Co or Ni and can be synthesized from a broad range of transition metals (TMs), particularly those earth-abundant ones, e.g., iron (Fe), manganese (Mn), and titanium (Ti). However, their capacity fade during cycling presents a major challenge. Li-excess chemical composition is necessary to facilitate a three-dimensional (3D) Li percolation network for facile Li-ion transport in the DRX lattice. Such Li-excess composition constrains the content of redox-active TM in the DRX compound and also enables oxygen (O) redox during the electrochemical process. The O redox is much less reversible compared to TM redox, and a high level of O redox activity in the DRX oxides usually triggers significant O loss from the crystal lattice, and consequently, severe capacity fade after cycling. By using fluorine anion (F-) substitution for oxygen anion (O2-), fluorination can increase the amount of low-valence redox-active TM without sacrificing Li content in the DRX compound. Overall, it has been noticed that partial fluorine (F) substitution into oxygen (O) lattice appears to be an effective strategy for improving the cycling stability, but the underlying atomistic mechanism remains unclear.
